verdict.rationale: Stripe's ACS lets sellers publish a structured catalog (CSV feed with product/variant/price/availability rows) that agent-side integrations can ingest, and checkout completion is surfaced via shared payment tokens / checkout sessions, giving developers a path to read offer data and reach checkout. But the read/discovery path is not an open universal API — it requires seller onboarding, region gating (US/Canada/select EU only), an explicit Open Commerce Agreement between agent and seller, and much of it (embedded checkout, agent-as-intermediary) is still private preview. Missing for 10: a public, unauthenticated read endpoint for arbitrary listed products, confirmation that variant/availability data is queryable in real time (vs daily/15-min batch feeds), and evidence the checkout-link discovery works outside gated OCA relationships.
